name: Hafnium
affiliation_detail:
According to DOJ indictment, HAFNIUM/Silk Typhoon operates on behalf of China's Ministry of State Security (MSS), specifically the Shanghai State Security Bureau (SSSB). On July 8, 2025, the DOJ unsealed an indictment charging two Chinese nationals: Xu Zewei (徐泽伟), employed by Shanghai Powerock Network Co. Ltd.; and Zhang Yu (张宇), employed by Shanghai Firetech Information Science and Technology Company, Ltd. Both, according to the indictment, operated under SSSB direction.
Shanghai Powerock shut down on April 7, 2021 — approximately one month after Microsoft publicly attributed the Exchange Server attacks to HAFNIUM and China. Xu Zewei subsequently moved to Chaitin Tech (another cybersecurity firm) and later to Shanghai GTA Semiconductor Ltd.
entity_name: Shanghai Firetech Information Science and Technology Company, Ltd.
description:
According to the U.S. DOJ indictment, HAFNIUM/Silk Typhoon is a Chinese state-sponsored cyber espionage group directed  by the MSS's Shanghai State Security Bureau (SSSB). 
The group was first described in March 2021 when Microsoft attributed the exploitation of four zero-day vulnerabilities in Microsoft Exchange Server. The campaign,  intially utilizing stolen credential or Microsoft Exchange Server zero day vulnerabilities, deployed web shells for persistent access to emails and sensitive data from government agencies, defense contractors, law firms, universities, and infectious disease researchers. (Microsoft, 2021)
During the COVID-19 pandemic, HAFNIUM targeted American universities conducting vaccine research, attempting to steal COVID-19 research data. (U.S. DOJ, 2021) More recently, the group targeted IT supply chain: Microsoft's March 2025 report documented Silk Typhoon compromising IT services providers, remote monitoring and management companies, and managed service providers to reach downstream customer environments. (Microsoft, 2025)
In July 2025, the DOJ unsealed indictments against two HAFNIUM operators — Xu Zewei and Zhang Yu — employed by Shanghai Powerock and Shanghai Firetech respectively. Xu was arrested on July 3, 2025, at Milan's Malpensa Airport by Italian law enforcement acting on a U.S. warrant. He was extradicted to the USA in April 2026. Zhang Yu remains at large.
SentinelLabs research (2025) revealed that Shanghai Firetech registered over 10 patents for intrusive data collection technologies, including remote automated evidence collection software, Apple computer forensics, router evidence collection, hard drive decryption, and remote cellphone evidence collection.

campaigns.name: COVID-19 Vaccine Research Espionage
campaigns.description: Beginning in February 2020 as the pandemic emerged, HAFNIUM operators targeted American universities conducting COVID-19 vaccine research. The U.S. DOJ indictment stated this campaign was aimed at "stealing groundbreaking COVID-19 research" on behalf of the CCP.

campaigns.name: Microsoft Exchange Server Mass Exploitation
campaigns.description:
HAFNIUM's most notorious campaign. The group initially gained stealthy access to U.S. government and organizational emails through zero-day exploitation of four Exchange Server vulnerabilities (ProxyLogon chain) starting in late 2020. Microsoft disclosed and patched the vulnerabilities on March 2, 2021. Between Microsoft's alert to partners (February 23) and public disclosure, other Chinese groups began mass exploitation at scale (February 28). The FBI assessed the campaign targeted over 60,000 U.S. entities and successfully compromised more than 12,700. Web shells deployed during exploitation provided persistent access even after patches were applied.
On July 19, 2021, the U.S., EU, UK, NATO, and allied nations issued a coordinated attribution with high confidence to PRC MSS-affiliated actors.

campaigns.name: Telecom and ISP Targeting (Tarrask)
campaigns.description: HAFNIUM deployed the Tarrask defense evasion malware against telecommunications companies, ISPs, and data service companies. Tarrask abused Windows scheduled task mechanisms to maintain hidden persistence on compromised servers.

sources.title: Tarrask Malware Uses Scheduled Tasks for Defense Evasion

campaigns.name: Cloud Providers Campaign
campaigns.description: Since 2023, CrowdStrike observed HAFNIUM/Murky Panda targeting cloud environment,  "likely motivated by intelligence-collection requirements to gain access to sensitive information." CrowdStrike described the adversary as "cloud-conscious," for its abilities to operate in cloud environment.

sources.title: MURKY PANDA: A Trusted-Relationship Threat in the Cloud

campaigns.name: IT Supply Chain Campaign
campaigns.description: Microsoft documented HAFNIUM/Silk Typhoon's shift toward IT supply chain targeting, compromising IT services providers, RMM companies, and MSPs to reach downstream customer environments. The group used stolen API keys, compromised OAuth applications, and service principal abuse for lateral movement and data exfiltration. Victims included state and local government, IT services, and financial institutions.
